navigation/activity-bar.a11y:
A tablist (`aria-orientation`) of tabs with names, tooltips and `aria-keyshortcuts`; one tab stop on the active view.
↑ ↓ (or ← →, mirrored in RTL) / Home / End move, Enter / Space choose. Badges are read with the tab.

props: `{ id, label, icon, href, onSelect, siblings }`; a sibling is `{ id, label, icon, sub, href, onSelect, current }`
what stands between the crumbs; `false`: nothing
collapse the middle into the "…" menu when narrow; `false`: the path is clipped instead

navigation/breadcrumbs.notes:
```tsx
<Breadcrumbs items={path} separator="/" ellipsis="···" labels={{ more: "Folders in between", goTo: (name) => `Open next to ${name}` }} />
<Breadcrumbs items={path} separator={false} collapse={false} />
```

A sibling with `href` is a link (the router's Link: a middle click or "open in new tab" works), one with `onSelect`
a button. `current: true` marks the sibling the path goes through (tinted; the link of the open page has
`aria-current="page"` from the router), `sub` adds a quieter second line.

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs separator="/" items={[
  { id: "home", label: "March", href: "/" },
  { id: "forms", label: "Forms", siblings: sections.map((s) => ({ id: s.path, label: s.title, sub: s.desc, icon: s.icon, href: s.path, current: s.path === "/forms" })) },
  { id: "select", label: "Select", siblings: pagesOf("/forms").map((p) => ({ id: p.path, label: p.title, href: p.path, current: p.path === here })) },
]} />
```
navigation/breadcrumbs.a11y:
`nav` with a name around an ordered list; the last crumb has `aria-current="page"`. Separators are hidden from
assistive technology. Crumbs with siblings are menu buttons (`aria-haspopup="menu"`, arrows, Esc). Collapsed crumbs
are items of the "…" menu.

navigation/nav-menu.a11y:
A `<nav>` landmark with a label; the active link has `aria-current="page"`; group headers are buttons with
`aria-expanded`; the filter is a labelled search box. The narrow-screen drawer is opened by a labelled menu button and
closes with Escape or the scrim.

navigation/page-dots.a11y:
Interactive: a `group` of buttons, each named "Page n", the current one `aria-current="true"`. One tab stop (the
current dot); Left / Right (Up / Down when vertical, mirrored in right-to-left text), Home and End move and select.
The target around a dot is larger than the dot. Read-only: one image named "Page n of N" (or hidden with
`decorative`). Reduced motion: no size transition.

navigation/pagination.notes:
```tsx
<Pagination bind:page={$page} pages={20} prev="‹ Back" next="More ›" gap="·" color="brand-blue"
  label="Result pages" labels={{ previous: "Previous page", next: "Next page", page: (n) => `Page ${n}` }} />
<Pagination bind:page={$page} pages={5} controls={false} />          // numbers only
<Pagination variant="simple" bind:page={$page} total={134} size={$size} sizes={[20, 50]} onSize={(n) => $size = n} />
<Pagination variant="simple" hasPrev={$before != null} hasNext={$after != null} onPrev={older} onNext={newer} />   // cursor mode
<Pagination variant="simple" bind:page={$slide} pages={12} status={(p, n) => `${p} / ${n}`} prev={arrowLeft} next={arrowRight} />
```
navigation/pagination.a11y:
A `<nav>` named "Pagination"; the current page has `aria-current="page"`; Previous / Next have accessible names and are
disabled at the ends; the ellipsis is hidden from assistive technology. Simple variant: the default buttons carry their
text ("Previous", "Next"), your own content gets the accessible name, and the range text is a polite live region.

navigation/period-nav.a11y:
A `group` named "Period" (your `labels.group`). The arrows are icon buttons named "Previous" / "Next" (your labels),
the today button is a text button; all are in the Tab order and work with Enter / Space. The title is plain text: a
host that wants changes read gives it a live element (Calendar does). In right-to-left text the chevrons point the
other way while "previous" stays first in reading order.

navigation/stepper.notes:
```tsx
<Stepper steps={steps} current={$step} onSelect={(i) => $step = i} panels={panels} highlight={false}
  counter={(i, n) => `${n - i - 1} left`} labels={{ back: "Previous", next: "Continue", step: (i, n) => `Stage ${i + 1} / ${n}` }} />
```
navigation/stepper.a11y:
The steps are the Steps list (`aria-current="step"`, buttons when `onSelect` is set). The panel frame is a polite
live region named "Step n of m"; the leaving panel is hidden from assistive technology while it fades. Back / Next
are buttons that control the panel. Reduced motion: the highlight jumps and panels switch at once.

navigation/steps.a11y: An ordered list; the current step has `aria-current="step"`; with `onSelect` each step is a native button.

navigation/tabs.notes:
```tsx
<Tabs tabs={tabs} motion="slide" indicator={false} />
<Tabs tabs={tabs} motion={(panel, dir) => animate(panel, [{ opacity: 0, transform: `translateX(${dir * 40}px)` }, { opacity: 1, transform: "none" }], { duration: 300 })} />
```

A tab can carry an icon, the "changed" dot and a close mark; `actions` sits at the end of the bar:

```tsx
<Tabs variant="pill" onClose={(id) => close(id)} actions={<IconButton icon={plus} label="New file" onClick={add} />} tabs={[
  { id: "a", label: "index.ts", icon: code, dirty: () => $changed, closable: true, content: () => <Editor /> },
  { id: "b", label: "Preview", icon: eye, disabled: () => !$ok, title: () => ($ok ? null : "Fix the errors first") },
]} />
```

`TabList` is the strip alone (the same tabs, roving focus and selection, no panel), for a strip that drives something
else: `<TabList tabs={views} value={$view} onSelect={(id) => $view = id} orientation="vertical" activation="manual" />`.
It also takes `tabId`, `controls` (the id of the panel), `wrap(button, tab)` (e.g. a Tooltip around each tab) and
`variant="none"` (no look: your own classes through `tabProps`).
navigation/tabs.a11y:
`role="tablist"` with `role="tab"` buttons (`aria-selected`, `aria-controls`) and one `role="tabpanel"` labelled by the
active tab. Only the active tab is a Tab stop; ← → Home End move and activate (mirrored in RTL). Disabled tabs are
skipped. A closable tab is closed with Delete (`aria-keyshortcuts`); its close mark is a pointer shortcut hidden from
assistive technology, and the "changed" dot has an accessible name. `actions` stay outside the tab list. Reduced
motion: the panel switches without motion.
